steps.text: In a large bowl, combine the tomatoes, cheese, onion, oil, vinegar, basil, and salt and pepper to taste. Toss and chill for 1 hour. Serve on large platter.

raw_recipe.headline: Insalata Caprese I
raw_recipe.description: Thick wedges of ripe tomatoes, fresh Mozzarella and slices of red onion are tossed in olive oil and vinegar and sprinkled with chopped, fresh basil. Chill and eat.
raw_recipe.name: Insalata Caprese I

recipeInstructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the tomatoes, cheese, onion, oil, vinegar, basil, and salt and pepper to taste. Toss and chill for 1 hour. Serve on large platter.

review.reviewBody: Tomatoes and fresh basil are a classic combination! It doesn't get much better or much simpler that this - it's absolutely delicious! I decreased the onion and I probably could have left it out altogether. I plated this vs. tossing in all in a bowl. Plus, I NEVER chill it, but rather leave it at room temperature. It's so fresh and so good it could be a meal in and of itself! It's perfect with a a side a crusty Italian bread and a good wine. A definite crowd pleaser!

Super easy and super delicious. I agree w/previous reviewers' posts about using more EVOO and less balsamic vinegar. I used twice as much oil than vinegar. I added about a tbsp. of garlic pepper and a tsp. of sea salt. After sitting overnight, the next day's leftover batch tasted even better! If you have the chance, let it sit overnight.

Made with only fresh mozzarella, sweet onions, caprese tomatoes, fresh basil and olive oil. Sprinkled kosher salt on the sliced mozzarella, onions and tomatoes and let them drain several hours (in separate colanders) before combining. Really good.

N.J. is known for growing the tastiest tomatoes in the country and we all know never to refrigerate these red beauties, as they will lose their flavor. After combining the ingredients, including garlic, I just let the mixture sit on my counter to absorb all the wonderful flavors. Ten minutes before serving I added the cheese. Thanks so much Kathy for a great side!!!!
Made this for my daughter's grad party but chopped everything together and let it marinate. It was really pretty and delicious!

These were awesome. Fresh GARDEN tomatoes are a must - the store variety don't cut it. I sliced my tomatoes in thick slices then seasoned them with salt and pepper, topped with a slice of fresh mozzarella and onion then drizzled olive oil and balsamic vinegar glaze (a little thicker than regular balsamic). Topped with fresh basil thinly sliced into ribbons. Everyone loved them and it was a quick and easy summer appetizer.
Wonderful, put on a flat bread or pizza crust and broil to melt the cheese!!Yum! I used smoked mozzarella and it was even better!

Very good salad. I only rated a 4 because I changed it up a bit by adding a clove of minced fresh garlic and making the dressing using 3 parts extra virgin olive oil to 1 part of the balsamic vinegar. 1/2 balsamic and 1/2 oil makes it very tart and overpowering. Make sure the balsamic is the best you can buy, the older the better, the more syrupy it is, the better. Trader Joe's sells a very nice aged balsamic for less than $10 a bottle.

Admittedly, I picked this recipe based on a photo. I liked the cut up cherry/grape tomatoes for a "dish-able" side dish. This was delicious. I cubed fresh mozz., halved red & yellow cherry tomatoes, chopped the basil (chiffonade, and thinly slice the onion. I mixed those and then waited until just before travel time (taking dish to a gathering) to add the liquids. I'll definitely make this again. Thanks, katquilter!
Yummy! I made it following the recipe to the letter the first time and it was great. Then I took the advise of other reviewers and didn't refrigerate the tomatoes and it really enhanced the flavors.
These are really good! I put fresh minced garlic on mine and make it on a bed of romaine lettuce...I add grilled chicken a lot of times too!
This is our family’s summertime favorite! I eat it as a light meal! Delicious!!!
Made it Twice all my family like it so much
I used red wine vinegar because I was out of balsamic. It was amazing. Will make again for sure.
This is a good recipe if you like fresh mozzarella. The texture doesn't do much for me.
I made it for my Bible study group and they loved it. We were having Stromboli and this made a perfect side dish!!
very very good. It is sitting on the counter letting the flavors blend now. Will serve with salmon fillets (left over from last night) and some toasted garlic bread. I have high hopes.
Yummy! leah

This was ssssoooooooo yummy! So easy, so fresh, and gorgeous! I will be making this over and over again. What a treat! I did not use all of the oil and balsalmic vinegar it called for. 1/3 cup oil seemed like a lot. I used 3 TBS, but I think you could use even less. Great salad!

I suppose this is just personal taste, but personally I found this to be too oily, not vinegary enough, and very bland. More onions or garlic could have helped I think. I put in more vinegar than called for and still was disappointed. It was still edible, so I'll give two stars.
